# Faker: 25 undocumented behaviour regressions to track down without a test suite

I have been generating sample data with this library for a while, and after upgrading I am getting wrong answers across a wide spread of what I ask for. The repository has received 25 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about how I call it changed: the same requests that used to come back right now come back wrong, and one or two do not come back at all. Here is everything I have pinned down by watching what I get.

Anything that has to add up arithmetically no longer does. A twenty-digit Spanish account number is often not twenty digits at all — a stray minus sign turns up in the middle — and the international form built from it fails validity checking, because the two verification digits sitting between the branch part and the rest disagree with the digits around them. An eighteen-digit Mexican account number I know to be good, fed to the library's own validity check for that format, comes back reported as not valid, so that verification digit is being worked out under the wrong rule. Nine-digit US routing numbers are still nine digits long but no longer satisfy their checksum. The twelve-digit Swedish personal number, with and without the dash, ends in a digit that contradicts its own checksum, although the eight leading characters still spell a real date.
